chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I was sitting with a judge from the judges of the city when two men came to him. One of them said: I hired this man to take me to the market on such and such a day, but he did not do it.' The judge said: 'There is no wage for him.' The man said: 'So I called him and said to him: O servant of Allah, it is not for you to take his right (by keeping the full wage), and I said to the worker: It is not for you to take all that you agreed upon, so reconcile between yourselves.'

key_terms.فَتَرَادَّا: So reconcile / settle between each other

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hiring and payment if the worker fails to complete the agreed task?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrates a dispute over a hired donkey where the animal failed to arrive, illustrating the Shia legal principle of *ikhtiyar* (mutual choice) in contracts. While the judge initially ruled no wage was due for unperformed work, the Imam advised against strict forfeiture, encouraging the parties to settle fairly between themselves to preserve equity (*adl*) and avoid rigid literalism. This highlights the importance of amicable resolution (*sulh*) in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence.
